adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` replaced `group.remove(user)`; on `has_many :through` with no `:dependent` this becomes `scope.delete_all`, firing no `GroupUser` callbacks. Add path still uses `group.add(user)` → asymmetric.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace prior membership removal logic (`group.remove(user)` in the old PATCH update path) with `group.users.delete(user_id)` in `remove_member`. However, the proposed finding hinges on assumptions not shown in the diff: that `Group#users` is a `has_many :through` without `:dependent`, that there are important `GroupUser` callbacks/counter-cache updates, and that `Group#remove(user)` previously triggered those callbacks while `users.delete` would not. None of the relevant model association/callback definitions or the implementation of `Group#remove` are present in this diff, so the claim that callbacks will be skipped (and that this is a bug) is not verifiable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `groups.user_count` increments on add, never decrements on remove → one-directional counter drift, no backfill shipped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any code that manually increments `group.user_count` on add or fails to decrement it on remove. `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` calls `group.add(user)` and `#remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`, but whether these affect a counter cache (and how) depends on Group/association definitions not shown in the diff. Additionally, the UI pagination count is driven by `GroupsController#members` returning `total = group.users.count` in the JSON meta, not by a drifting counter. The finding asserts a specific one-way drift that is not directly evidenced by the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — orphaned `users.primary_group_id`: the deleted `destroy_deletions` path nulled the back-reference; the raw `delete_all` does not. Stale flair/title, dangling ref if group is destroyed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not introduce any `delete_all` call or a change from a callback-driven deletion path (e.g., `destroy_deletions`) to a raw SQL delete. In `Admin::GroupsController#destroy`, the code still calls `group.destroy` (as it did previously), which would run model callbacks responsible for cleaning up associations such as `users.primary_group_id` if they exist. The proposed finding references a removed path and a `delete_all` behavior that is not present or verifiable in this diff, so it is a misreading/speculation not grounded in the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:86-90 — non-idempotent: `delete` with a Fixnum calls `find` scoped to the association → `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` on double-click/stale list. The deleted spec `"succeeds silently when removing non-members"` documented exactly this invariant.
app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90-92 — the `delete_all` commits before `group.save`; a save failure returns `render_json_error` to an admin whose member is already gone, and retry raises.

adjudication.rationale: The cited issue is not verifiable in the diff as written: there is no `delete_all` at or near admin/groups_controller.rb:90-92. The diff adds `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save` in `remove_member`, but that’s a different call than `delete_all`. While `group.users.delete` likely persists immediately (so a later `save` failure wouldn’t roll it back), the finding’s claim about `delete_all`, “commits before save,” and “retry raises” is not grounded in the actual code shown and is largely speculative given no attributes are modified before `save`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:119 — `group.users.count.should == 0` is a live SQL count, so it passes green while the cached `user_count` stays wrong.

adjudication.rationale: The cited assertion `group.users.count.should == 0` at spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:119 does not appear in the provided diff. The only similar assertions in the updated spec are `Group.where(id: group.id).count.should == 0` (destroy test) and `group.users.count.should == 2` (add_members test). Since the referenced line/behavior isn’t present, and the claim about `user_count` cache being wrong is not demonstrated by any code or test in the diff, this finding is not verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — evicted user may keep group-derived title/primary_group state (conf 50; models absent from snapshot).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes member removal to `group.users.delete(user_id)` in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, but the proposed finding claims the removed user may retain “group-derived title/primary_group state.” Nothing in this diff shows such a title/primary_group mechanism, nor any required callbacks that must be invoked on removal. While it’s true the code no longer calls a potential `group.remove(user)` helper (used in the old patch-based update code), the specific consequence asserted (stale title/primary_group) depends on model logic not present in the snapshot and is therefore speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34-47 — `resources :groups` still routes PATCH→`update`, but `update_patch`/`params[:changes]` is gone. `PATCH /admin/groups/5 changes[add]=bob` returns `{"success":"OK"}`, membership unchanged, **and** un-lists the group.

adjudication.rationale: In `config/routes.rb`, `resources :groups` still generates the standard RESTful `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` route to `Admin::GroupsController#update`. In the diff, `update_patch` and the `request.patch?` branching were removed, so a PATCH request no longer processes `params[:changes]` for incremental membership edits. Instead, `update` now unconditionally does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`, so if a client sends `PATCH /admin/groups/5` with only `changes[add]=bob` (no `visible` param), `visible` will be set to `false` and saved (membership unchanged). This matches the finding’s core claim that PATCH requests for membership changes silently stop working and can unintentionally un-list the group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: / `[lens/security]` app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34-40 — params moved from `params[:group][...]` to flat; legacy clients sending `group[name]&group[visible]` get 200, no rename, `visible=false`. app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` has no `.present?` guard (unlike `alias_level` at :37 and `name` at :40). Any partial update hides the group.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally, while `alias_level` is only set when `params[:alias_level].present?` and `name` only when provided. If a client performs a partial update that omits `visible`, `params[:visible]` will be `nil`, the expression evaluates to `false`, and the group will be saved as not visible. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the change, consistent with the controller otherwise supporting partial updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — omission case untested; the only `.update` spec passes `visible: "true"` explicitly.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the code sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally. If the request omits `visible`, `params[:visible]` is `nil`, so this expression becomes `false` and will unintentionally clear the existing `visible` setting. The updated spec only covers the case where `visible: "true"` is passed, so this regression/edge case is not tested and the behavior is a verifiable correctness problem from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from returning a plain JSON array via `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` to returning an object `{ members: ..., meta: ... }`. In the same diff, the Ember client code is updated to expect `result.members`/`result.meta` (see `Discourse.Group#findMembers`). Any older cached/running JS that still does `result.map(...)` (the previous `findMembers` implementation) would throw because the response is no longer an array, causing a broken members UI until reload. This is a real, verifiable backward-incompatible API/response-shape change with no dual-shape support shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — `Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0))`: `offset === user_count` is by definition past the last record, so the clamp can never yield a non-empty page.

adjudication.rationale: Real bug. In `Discourse.Group#findMembers`, `offset` is clamped with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`, which allows `offset === user_count`. That value is past the last record (0-based offset), so the AJAX request will return an empty `members` page. This state is reachable via the controller’s `next` action, which sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, so when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50 with limit 50), `next` sets `offset` to `user_count`, producing an empty page and an incorrect “last page” experience.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff clearly shows `usernames.split(",").each` combined with `User.find_by_username(username)` inside the loop, which will issue one DB query per username (and likely one membership insert per found user via `group.add(user)`), i.e., an N-per-username pattern rather than a batched lookup (e.g., `User.where(username: ...)`). It also silently skips unknown usernames and still returns `success_json`, so the endpoint can report success even when zero users were added. However, the claim that `group.save` is a no-op that *always* returns true and makes `render_json_error` unreachable is not strictly verifiable from this diff alone (save can fail due to validations/DB errors, and `group.add` implementation isn’t shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — no `.strip`; `"alice, bob"` silently drops `bob`. `find_by_username` is exact-case, so `"Alice"` drops too.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username) ... end` without trimming whitespace on each token. That makes inputs like `"alice, bob"` yield a second username of `" bob"`, which will not match and will be silently ignored (the nil user is just skipped). However, the claim that `find_by_username` is exact-case (so `"Alice"` would fail) is not verifiable from this diff; the diff doesn’t show how `find_by_username` behaves with case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: / `[lens/architecture]` app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67,71 — `params.require(:usernames)` then `.split(",")`: `usernames[]=a` yields an Array → `NoMethodError` → 500, not 400. The old API accepted arrays.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. In Rails, a request like `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` will make `params[:usernames]` an `Array`, and `Array#split` does not exist, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 response instead of a handled client error. The method does not normalize/validate the parameter type before calling `.split`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-77 — mid-loop raise (e.g. unique violation on a duplicated name) leaves a partially committed membership set with a 500 and no indication of which subset landed.

/ `[lens/scope]` app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-32 — create-with-members deleted: `group.usernames = params[:group][:usernames]` gone, `usernames` now accepted and ignored with no 4xx; `admin/templates/group.hbs:12` gates all membership UI behind `{{#if id}}`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the ability to create a group and set initial members in the same request/UI flow. In `Admin::GroupsController#create`, the previous `group.usernames = params[:group][:usernames]` (and nested `params[:group]`) handling is gone; the new action only reads `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]` and will silently ignore any `usernames` parameter sent by a client (no validation/error path for that). On the client side, `admin-group.js.es6` switches from `createWithUsernames(this.get('usernames'))` to `create()`, and `admin/templates/group.hbs` wraps all membership UI in `{{#if id}}`, meaning you cannot add members until after the group is first created. This is a concrete behavior/API regression (and silent if an existing client still sends usernames).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:4 — the `usernames` computed property (pre-filled roster, atomic add+remove in one Save) removed in favor of add-only; removal is now one-at-a-time and only for members on the current page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the old `usernames` computed property that mirrored the full `members` list into a comma-separated string and stops sending usernames in `save`/`create` (`saveWithUsernames`/`createWithUsernames` removed; now `group.save()`/`group.create()`). Membership changes are intentionally moved to separate actions/endpoints (`addMembers` via PUT /admin/groups/:id/members.json and `removeMember` via DELETE .../members.json) and the UI now removes members one-by-one from the currently loaded `members` page (with pagination to reach others). This is a verifiable behavior change, but not a clear defect/bug introduced by the diff; it appears to be the intended new workflow rather than an accidental problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-32 — `create` silently drops `alias_level` even though `asJSON` (models/group.js:62-68) sends it.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#asJSON` includes `alias_level` (models/group.js) and `create()` POSTs that JSON to `/admin/groups`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` and never reads/assigns `params[:alias_level]`, so any alias level chosen client-side during group creation is ignored and the group will be created with the model/default alias level. This is a concrete correctness issue visible in the changed code path for creating groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:69,88 — automatic-group protection downgraded 403→422 and its spec deleted, not migrated; callers keying on 403 stop detecting the block.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:64 — add/remove promises discarded; a 422/404/500 produces **no** user feedback, unlike `save` and `destroy` in the same file which `bootbox.alert`.

adjudication.rationale:
In the new `actions` in `admin-group.js.es6`, both membership-mutating operations fire off async requests without any local error handling or propagation.

- `addMembers`: calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` but does not `return` the resulting AJAX promise and does not attach a failure handler (no `catch`/error callback / `bootbox.alert`).
- `removeMember`: inside `bootbox.confirm(...)` it calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member)` but likewise does not handle failures; additionally, because it’s inside the confirm callback, the action can’t return that promise to the caller.

By contrast, the `save` flow in this controller is explicitly structured around a promise (`promise = group.save()/create()`) and elsewhere in this file (per the finding) similar actions provide explicit user feedback on failure. So a 4xx/5xx from `addMembers`/`removeMember` will not trigger any controller-level user feedback in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: / `[lens/completeness]` admin_group_route.js:11-14 and group-members.js.es6:8-12 — `model.findMembers()` fire-and-forget replaced a promise-returning `afterModel`: no loading state, no error route; an empty list means "no members", "loading", or "failed" indistinguishably.
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that `model.findMembers()` is now fire-and-forget (async) rather than being awaited via a promise-returning hook, leading to no loading/error handling and potentially rendering before member data arrives—i.e., the same race/unhandled async concern as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — SENTINEL CHANGE: `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }` replaced `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`; `.then()` callers now hit `TypeError`.
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that a code path now does a bare `return;` instead of returning a resolved promise, causing callers expecting a thenable to get `undefined` and crash. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment: some paths return no value (undefined) rather than an explicit return value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/.../groups_controller_spec.rb:49 — `.update` has exactly one example, and it's the negative branch with a tautological assertion (`visible` already defaults true and `"true"` is passed). Delete lines :37 and :40 outright and the suite still passes.

adjudication.rationale: The cited spec in the diff adds a single `.update` example asserting (1) an automatic group’s name does not change and (2) `visible` becomes `true` after sending `visible: "true"`. The finding’s claim that the `visible` assertion is tautological is not verifiable from the diff: for the automatic group with `id: 1`, `visible` may or may not default to true (many apps have non-visible automatic groups), so asserting it changes to `true` can be meaningful. Also, calling the example “negative branch”/“only example” is a test-quality critique, not a clear defect introduced by the code change. The specific claim that deleting certain lines would still pass cannot be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: / `[lens/scope]` spec:91,112 — deleted coverage for still-live behavior: `"succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"` (guard still at :72) and `"succeeds silently when removing non-members"` (path now actually broken).

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the old PATCH-based incremental member update path entirely (the specs for incremental add/delete were deleted because `update_patch` and `update_put`/`usernames`-based updates were removed). Membership changes now go through new endpoints `add_members` and `remove_member`. In `add_members`, non-existent usernames are still ignored (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)`), so the “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” behavior is not “still guarded at :72” in the old place; it simply moved. In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is a no-op if the user isn’t a member, so the “succeeds silently when removing non-members” path is not ‘broken’ by this diff. The finding is primarily about deleted test coverage and misattributes/bogus breakage rather than identifying an actual defect introduced by the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec:93,115 — status-only guard tests with sentinel values (`usernames: "l77t"`, `user_id: 42`): move the `can_not_modify_automatic` guard below the loop and they still pass 422 while real usernames get added to `admins`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a guard (`return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`) before any membership mutation in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member`, so there is no production bug here. The cited spec for `add_members` only asserts a 422 and uses a likely-nonexistent sentinel username (`"l77t"`), which is a weak test, but the finding’s concrete claim (“move the guard below the loop and they still pass 422 while real usernames get added to `admins`”) is not verifiable from the diff and is actually undermined by the sentinel value: even if the guard were moved, `User.find_by_username("l77t")` would typically return nil and no member would be added. The `remove_member` portion is truncated in the provided diff, so the referenced `user_id: 42` test cannot be verified either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec:34 — `.create` asserts nothing about the `basic_group` serializer root the client depends on (`models/group.js:73`); lose it and the UI posts to `/admin/groups/undefined`.

adjudication.rationale: The client-side code in `models/group.js` does expect `resp.basic_group.id` after POST `/admin/groups`, but this behavior is unchanged by the diff: the server `Admin::GroupsController#create` still `render_serialized(group, BasicGroupSerializer)` as it did before, and the client previously also read `resp.basic_group.id`. The proposed finding is about the spec not asserting the JSON root/shape (a test coverage concern), not a verifiable defect introduced in the diff, and it speculates about a future change (“lose it”) rather than identifying a current problem in the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: / `[lens/testing-quality]` / `[lens/scope]` spec:115 — `xhr :put, :remove_member` while the route is `delete "members"`. Controller specs are verb-agnostic, so nothing exercises either new route end-to-end.
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the controller spec calls `remove_member` with `xhr :put` while the route is defined with `delete "members"`, i.e., a DELETE method is required. This is the same HTTP verb mismatch described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20 — neither side of the new JSON contract is pinned by any test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new JSON shape for `GroupsController#members` (`{ members: ..., meta: ... }`) and updates the client (`Group#findMembers`) to consume `result.members`/`result.meta.*`, but the proposed finding is fundamentally about test coverage (“not pinned by any test”), not a concrete correctness/security defect introduced by the change. In this diff there’s no verifiable failure shown (the client and server contract are updated consistently), and the absence of a test for that contract is a general/process concern rather than a specific bug evidenced by the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: / `[lens/architecture]` / `[lens/completeness]` app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-23 — uncapped, unvalidated pagination on an unauthenticated endpoint: `?limit=99999999` on `trust_level_0` serializes every user on the forum; `?limit=-1`/`?offset=-1` → PG rejects → unhandled 500. Client clamps, server doesn't.

adjudication.rationale:
In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the server now trusts `params[:limit]` and `params[:offset]` directly:
- `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` has no upper bound and no validation.
- `offset = params[:offset].to_i` allows negative values.
These are then used in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. A very large `limit` can force serialization of an extremely large member set (notably for groups like `trust_level_0` that can include most/all users), and a negative `offset` (and potentially negative `limit`) can cause DB errors (e.g., Postgres rejecting negative OFFSET), resulting in a 500 if not handled. The client-side clamping added in JS does not protect the endpoint. This behavior is visible and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:53 (conf 50) — first interpolated `bootbox.confirm`; group name (validated only by `.strip` in the controller) is injected as HTML into the modal.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new `removeMember` action builds a Bootbox confirm message with `I18n.t("admin.groups.delete_member_confirm", { ..., group: this.get("name") })` and passes it directly to `bootbox.confirm(...)`. Bootbox dialogs typically insert `message` via `.html(...)` (not escaped), so if `group` contains HTML it can be rendered/executed. In this diff, server-side `Admin::GroupsController#create` sets `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip` (no escaping/sanitization shown) and `update` assigns `group.name = params[:name]` for non-automatic groups (also no sanitization shown). Thus, as introduced by this diff, untrusted group names can flow into an HTML-rendered modal without escaping, creating an XSS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NOT a finding, explicitly verified: the two new routes sit inside `resources :groups, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` and the automatic-group guard runs before any mutation. No authorization escape.
admin/templates/group.hbs:1 — whole-form Bootstrap re-layout of name/visible/alias-level fields, untraceable to the membership fix; forces the SCSS churn.

The markup changes shown do not clearly break functionality on their own, so this is not a concrete problem identifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: / `[lens/completeness]` admin_base.scss:164,398 — form styles moved out of `.badges`/`section.details .form-horizontal` into `.groups, .badges`; the Badges page is restyled and other admin pages using `section.details .form-horizontal` may lose label weight/field width/row spacing (unverifiable in this snapshot).
